newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Jospin to outline policies on June 19.
newsitem.headline: France's Jospin to outline policies on June 19.

text.p: France's Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin will make his first policy statement to the National Assembly on June 19, aides said on Wednesday.
It was the first official confirmation of a date which had already been widely rumoured.

Aides said Jospin would outline his policies and announce key dates for implementing his programme -- a revised budget and a national conference on jobs, wages and working hours bringing together government, employers and trade unions.
The policy statement in the assembly is traditionally followed by a confidence vote.
Jospin is to meet his ministers on Thursday (0900 GMT) to set out priorities for the government action and prepare his policy statement.
Socialist parliamentarians who met Jospin on Wednesday said he had confirmed that he would present a revised budget to parliament.
"There will be a revised budget. But I can't tell you when," said Socialist MP Jean-March Ayrault.
He denied reports that he would skirt parliament by making his first moves by decree.
Jospin took power last week from Gaullist Alain Juppe following the left's June 1 parliamentary election victory.
